import cv2, numpy as np
ref = cv2.imread(r'$dir\input\input.png')
# reference is crane on green; make a rough subject mask (non-green)
hsv = cv2.cvtColor(ref, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
# green ~ hue 60 in opencv (0-179 ~ 60). #00FF00 -> H=60,S=255,V=255
b,g,r = cv2.split(ref.astype(int))
green_mask = (g>150)&(r<120)&(b<120)
subj = ~green_mask
ys,xs = np.where(subj)
print('ref subj bbox x',xs.min(),xs.max(),'y',ys.min(),ys.max(),'count',subj.sum())
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(r'$dir\input\input.mp4')
n=int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
# For each source frame, the crane is darker/whiter than sky; hard. Instead, compare ref subject pixels region.
# Find best matching frame by template-ish: compute where ref has subject, sample source frames, measure correlation of ref subject (in subject area) to source.
best=None
reff=ref.astype(np.float32)
for f in range(0,n,4):
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES,f); ok,img=cap.read()
    if not ok: continue
    d=np.abs(img.astype(np.float32)-reff)[subj].mean()
    if best is None or d<best[1]: best=(f,d)
print('best matching frame (lowest diff in subj area):',best)
cap.release()
"@
